--- title: "Nonsymbolic magnitude comparison" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · MATE_SEN_NUM_MAGNITUDES_NO_SIMB" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (E · Decision with response time; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_SEN_NUM_MAGNITUDES_NO_SIMB`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Comparación de magnitudes no simbólicas*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_SEN_NUM_MAGNITUDES_NO_SIMB.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Nonsymbolic magnitude comparison, from age 4 to 11 (4,115 administrations in 6 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .34. AUC .56–.65 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 10752 1744 1745 | | Battery | ORZA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 24 (10752); 16 (1744) according to the platform | | Task family | E · Decision with response time | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | Participants are required to “instantly” saying if the quantity of points shown in two pictures are the same or different without counting. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. La lámina se corta en pantallas estrechas. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=3} ![10752 · Magnitudes No Simbólicas](../../figuras/plataforma/10752.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 10752"} ![1744 · Subitizing - No Simbólico](../../figuras/plataforma/1744.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1744"} ![1745 · Línea Mental](../../figuras/plataforma/1745.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1745"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Comparing quantities measures **numerical magnitude processing**. In the **non-symbolic** version, the child sees two sets of dots and says whether they have the same number or not: this is attributed to the approximate number system, which estimates quantities without counting. In the **symbolic** version, the child compares two digits and chooses the larger: this requires accessing magnitude from the learned symbol. **What the evidence says:** - **Both are related to mathematics, the symbolic one somewhat more.** A meta-analysis of 45 articles (284 effects, 17,201 participants) estimates r = .30 for symbolic comparison and .24 for non-symbolic comparison. The relation is stronger with mental calculation and early mathematics [@schneider2017associations]. - **Symbolic knowledge better predicts arithmetic progress.** In 6-year-olds followed for 11 months, knowledge of Arabic numerals predicted arithmetic growth and magnitude comparison added nothing [@gobel2014arithmetic]. In 62 Spanish 4-year-olds, digits and arithmetic predicted later improvement of the approximate system, and not the other way round [@munez2024interrelations]. - **The dot task is not a pure measure.** Most children compare the sets by their visual features (size, area) more than by number [@clayton2019nonsymbolic]. The evidence for the approximate system as a causal basis of arithmetic is contradictory. Symbolic comparison is the strongest candidate for school screening. **What our data show.** - **Reliability.** The non-symbolic version has modest consistency (α = .63) and little stability across terms (ρ = .29–.38); the symbolic version, even less (ρ = .20–.21). At age 5, 25% of children reach the maximum in the non-symbolic version. - **Validity against mathematics.** They predict low arithmetic at ages 10–11 poorly (AUC .54–.61). Symbolic comparison at ages 10–11 correlates with arithmetic at the same time point (r = .32–.39) ([Numerical cognition](../../cognicion-numerica.en.qmd#sec-mate-criterio)). - **Validity against reading.** They are related to low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency as much as or more than to arithmetic (AUC .57–.70 for concurrent symbolic comparison; up to .77 for non-symbolic at age 5, with only 22 cases). They may reflect speed or attention more than number sense. The grouped codes are not homogeneous: the non-symbolic task mixes an examiner-administered version (1744) and a self-administered one (10752), and code 1745 is a number line task, not a comparison task. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|-----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.2| 1744| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 391| 387| 0| 17| | 4.3| 1744| 2011| 141|2015/16 | 745| 0| 745| 33| | 4.3| 1744| 2013| 191|2017/18 | 580| 570| 10| 23| | 5.1| 1744| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 781| 0| 781| 34| | 5.1| 1744| 2012| 182|2017/18 | 319| 315| 0| 16| | 5.3| 1744| 2010| 140|2015/16 | 679| 212| 465| 36| | 6.2| 10752| 2015| 950|2021/22 | 191| 0| 21| 8| | 7.1| 10752| 2014| 950|2021/22 | 199| 0| 0| 8| | 9.2| 10752| 2012| 949|2021/22 | 230| 50| 0| 11| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |-----:|----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 1744| 4.2| 387| 2012| 13.03| 2.42| 14| -1.11| 0.26| 2.84| | 1744| 4.3| 570| 2013| 13.06| 2.51| 14| -1.09| 0.35| 4.74| | 1744| 5.1| 315| 2012| 14.01| 2.18| 14| -1.17| 0.00| 8.57| | 1744| 5.3| 212| 2010| 15.28| 1.71| 16| -1.65| 0.00| 24.53| | 10752| 9.2| 50| 2012| 14.70| 2.25| 15| -0.92| 0.00| 22.00| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). coding under review) | 9.2| 226| 0.045| 0.731| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 9.2| 226| -0.165| 0.013| |School (ICC) | 9.2| 230| 0.183| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Nonsymbolic magnitude comparison” (codes 10752, 1744 and 1745; ORZA battery) assesses nonsymbolic number sense. Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 17 items. The time limit is 60 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 14 sessions, from 4 to 11 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .63 (N = 2,210, 17 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 6 months) was ρ = .34 (median of 2 session pairs; range .29–.38). Stability across time points was ρ = .29–.38. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .56–.63. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 4.2 (form 1744), 4.3 (form 1744), 5.3 (form 1744): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - Ceiling effect at 5.3 (form 1744), 9.2 (form 10752) (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - The task has several forms that never coincide at the same time point: their equivalence cannot be checked; norms are given by form. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
